query: A Page for Thornwick There's a space in the corner of your yearbook page where a friend's message should go, and a green-sealed letter on your desk that came this morning: "Four years of rivalry, four hundred letters. Leave me the corner. Insufferable to the end, T." Leave Tamsin the corner You send the page over the hills by the evening owl. It comes back by morning, a green seal pressed into the corner, which is not allowed, and two lines you'll know by heart for the rest of your life. Save it for the spring meeting You write back that the corner can wait: you'll fill it in person, at the town halfway between, in the spring, with biscuits. Tamsin's reply says "Coward" and "Yes" in the same line.

results.title: After Graduation
results.excerpt:
After Graduation
Tamsin's letter has a map on the back with two towns circled: Lumenhold and Thornwick, and a line between them. "After graduation, there'll be no school to be rivals for. What are we, then?" Under it, smaller: "Don't answer that. Answer it."
"Friends. Obviously."
